newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar up on mark despite G7, Eurobourses weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar up on mark despite G7, Eurobourses weak.

text.p: By Peter Griffiths

The dollar headed higher in European trading on Tuesday, breaking through 1.67 marks, and shrugging off weekend signals from the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations that it had risen far enough.

On the bourses, leading European shares were generally weaker in a predictable mark down after a 49 point overnight slide on Wall Street. Stock market sentiment was in marked contrast to Monday trading, which saw no fewer than eight European bourses hit new inter-day highs.

Currency traders said the dollar's climb was supported by continuing worries about the German economy. The dollar was also firm against the yen, but fears of possible intervention by the Bank of Japan to curb its rise were having a damping effect.
Last weekend a statement from G7 finance chiefs said currency "misalignments" had now been corrected, but it shunned talk of intervention to hold the dollar down.
"Japanese officials will continue to talk a stable yen, but I think the dollar will remain pretty well underpinned near term," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.,
The dollar touched 1.6710 marks in late morning, well up from late Monday's European level of 1.6571. Dollar/yen was at the day's best, at around 123.30, up from late Monday's 122.83.
"The market's concluding, and I think rightly so, that G7 was not an absolute, definitive watershed," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
"So long as the G7 is not going to change its monetary policy, the dollar is likely to push higher."
It was not only against the dollar that the mark was weak and sterling romped to a fresh high of nearly 2.74 marks, its best level since September, 1992.
The London stock market, Europe's busiest, was trading down a quarter of a percent by late morning. Dealers believed, however, the blue chip FTSE's decline would be shortlived.
"The Dow had a bad day yesterday and we've not really
been hit too badly," one dealer said. "This market just does not want to go down at the moment. It will take a pretty sharp drop in the U.S. for the bears to resurface."

Recent evidence that British inflationary pressures are modest continued to underpin the market's conviction that British interest rates will not be increased soon and the favourable interest rate picture has convinced some strategists that the FTSE's five percent advance so far this year has further to go before any significant correction.
The FTSE 100, which on Monday finished just 0.1 point below its record close of 4,307.8 set last Friday, was down 10 points points at 4,297.7 by noon gmt .

In Frankfurt the strength of the dollar -- which is good for German exports -- almost managed to outweigh the negative effect of the fall on Wall Street and the DAX index of leading shares was flat at midday.
German trading volumes were low however because Tuesday was a half-day pre-Lent holiday in Frankfurt.
In Paris, French stocks managed to open higher but
quickly fell into negative territory, under pressure from Wall Street's drop and strong resistance at the 2,600 level.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down a quarter of a percent at noon gmt. Despite the losses, traders said the French market was underpinned to some degree by firmness in bond prices and in the dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6705 marks and 123.30 yen compared with 1.6571 marks and 122.83 yen in late European trading on Monday
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 10.0 at 4,297.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 6.58 at 2,588.67.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 3.2 at 3,187.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $338.85, its lowest level since April 22, 1993 and against $340.40 previously. Silver, taking a back seat to gold, was off a cent at $4.94.
